## PM claim + dispatch order — R27

Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Branch: `claude/issue-5490-per-chunk-budgets`.

### This card is already a ruling. ⛔ Nothing here is open.

It was written by the triage seat **executing the maintainer's #5468 ruling** (2026-08-21, verbatim 「其他接受」): **A now + C next, B rejected.** The aggregate ceiling stays as shipped in PR #5466; this card delivers **C** — per-chunk budgets, so a single chunk cannot grow unnoticed inside aggregate headroom.

⛔ **Option B (a main-comparison ratchet) is rejected** and must not be reintroduced, for two recorded reasons: its merge-queue **double-ejection** failure mode, and per-PR build cost. If the implementation starts to feel like it wants a comparison against `main`, that is a signal to stop and report — not to build it.

### ⚠️ The sequencing caveat is binding — check it before measuring

The ruling carries a recorded caveat: **if #5325 / #5359 (the cleave work) has landed, set the per-chunk lines after it, not before.**

**Check that first.** Baselines measured against a pre-cleave closure would be wrong the moment the cleave lands, and a budget set too high is a gate that cannot fail. Report which state you found and which you measured against.

### What to build

Per-chunk **gzipped** ceilings in `scripts/__tests__/check-eager-closure-budget.test.ts` (or a sibling in the same gauge), for at minimum:

| chunk | card's figure |
|---|---|
| `vendor-objectstack` | 1,493 KB / **38%** of closure |
| `framework` | 484 KB |
| `ui-components` | 380 KB |

Set at **truthful current state + small headroom**, the same discipline as the aggregate ceiling. ⛔ **No unilateral lowering** — this is a ratchet, not an optimisation target, and lowering it below measured reality turns a budget into a bug report.

⚠️ **Re-measure all three.** Those figures are from 2026-08-21 and this repo has moved a great deal; every inherited number tonight has been stale.

### ⭐ The requirement that decides whether this gate is worth anything

> Chunk names/sizes come from the shipped gauge's **own measurement** (the `eager-closure` report), not hardcoded expectations that rot — **pin the mapping loudly if a chunk disappears or renames.**

That last clause is the whole design. A per-chunk budget keyed on a chunk name that no longer exists is **vacuously green** — the budget passes because it is measuring nothing. So:

- If a budgeted chunk name is **absent** from the report, the gate must **FAIL**, not skip. Predict and prove it: rename or remove a budgeted chunk name and confirm the gate reds naming it.
- If the report yields **zero** chunks, the gate must **FAIL**. A collapsed measurement must never read as under-budget.
- Put the measured sizes in the verdict line, not just pass/fail, so a reader sees headroom rather than a tick.

**Positive control**: raise one chunk past its ceiling (or lower a ceiling below measured) and confirm the gate reds naming that chunk and both numbers. Predict each direction before running; prove mutations on disk by anchored counts, never an editor's exit code; restore via `git checkout HEAD --` plus the explicit path with an empty `git diff HEAD`.

### Scope

The budget test and whatever the gauge needs to expose per-chunk numbers. ⛔ Do not change chunking, ⛔ do not change the aggregate ceiling, ⛔ do not attempt the cleave work (#5325 / #5359).

Root vitest only (objectui#3378). Exit codes captured by redirect before any pipe. ⚠️ Derive the gate list from `package.json` and `.github/workflows/` rather than from this order.

⚠️ This gate needs a **real build** to measure. Say plainly what happens if it runs against an unbuilt tree — ⛔ it must not silently pass. That exact false-green has bitten three of this seat's devs tonight on a different gate (`check:doc-snippets` prints "NOT run" and exits 0).
